solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: She might learn from her sister

definitions.text: She might learn from her sister

parts.words: She might learn from her sister
parts.note: reads like a younger girl learning from an older sibling, but a Sister is a senior hospital nurse who trains trainees on the ward

explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a Sister is the senior nurse in charge of a ward, so the family reading is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee on a nursing course is taught on the wards by the senior nurse called Sister.

indicators.note: during says the welcome sits within the other letters
a rescheduled meeting is rearranged, so the letters of tryst are reordered

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting of welcome

explanation.surface: A secret lovers' meeting is moved, with a welcome greeting in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: Ave, Latin for hail, is a crossword favourite for a greeting or welcome; the tryst is the lovers' meeting being moved.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque imitation, a mocking disguise of the real thing; the word comes from dressing in disguise.

clue.text: Stupid spending day at back of ship

parts.note: aft is the nautical term for the rear or stern of a ship

explanation.surface: It was foolish to spend a day at the stern of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: daft is a British informal word for silly or foolish.

clue.text: Another rook, leaving egg behind, fluttered over the country

indicators.note: fluttered suggests the bird's letters are flapping about into a new order
leaving egg behind says that letter is taken out of the words

parts.note: an egg is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Another bird abandons its egg and flies off over the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving egg behind' drops one O from ANOTHERROOK, then 'fluttered' rearranges ANTHERROOK.
explanation.definitionFit: North Korea is an Asian nation, so the country fits it as a description.

parts.note: looks like an antique gramophone, but the player is the small part that actually plays a disc

explanation.definitionFit: On a gramophone the stylus, a fine point, runs in the groove to play the record.

indicators.note: out says the way is spread open to take the next word inside

parts.note: a route is a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: Finding a way out is part of the daily round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way out' looks like an exit, but 'out' is the signal that the way is opened up to take what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a regular sequence of things done each day, the same round.

clue.text: Where to sell things out of the country

definitions.text: Where to sell things out of the country

parts.words: Where to sell things out of the country
parts.note: could be a rural shopping spot, but means a foreign destination for goods

explanation.definitionFit: A trade outlet abroad receives goods shipped from the home country.

clue.text: Nosh cooked in unfinished hut on island

indicators.note: in places the cooked letters inside the short hut
unfinished means the hut lacks its final letter
cooked suggests food is worked over, so the letters of nosh are rearranged

explanation.surface: Food is prepared in a half-built shack on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Nosh is British slang for food, so 'cooked' fits the surface while signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Honshu is the largest of the islands that make up Japan.

clue.text: Drink firm has the French backing

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: backing tells us the French word is read in reverse after the firm

parts.note: LA is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: A soft-drinks company has French investors supporting it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cola is a sweet fizzy soft drink, so drink is its general category.

parts.note: strength and force are synonyms
to siphon liquid is to pump it out, so siphon gives pump

explanation.surface: A plumber notes that a powerful siphon serves to clear blocked pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of pump drives water under pressure, which is used for clearing blockages from pipes.

parts.note: the apostle Peter's name means rock, and this Russian city bears his name

explanation.definitionFit: The Russian city was named for the apostle whose name means rock in Greek.

indicators.note: first says the check word comes before the hesitation in the answer

parts.note: to check something is to test it
ER is the sound a speaker makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone nervously inspects an awning before putting it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' places TEST ahead of ER, although the clue mentions the hesitation first.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tester is the canopy over a four-poster bed or a pulpit.

definitions.meaning: more like a spicy hot pepper dish, the comparative of a word for chilli-like
more cold, the comparative of a word meaning cold

explanation.definitionFit: The same comparative reads as more peppery from chilli and as colder from the adjective meaning cold.

clue.text: I combat mob rioting — with this?

definitions.text: I combat mob rioting — with this?

indicators.note: rioting suggests disorder, so these letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what weapon they would need to fight a rioting crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' rearranges ICOMBATMOB, and the whole clue describes an extreme way to fight a mob.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear weapon would be a drastic, absurd means of fighting a crowd of rioters.

clue.text: On it quite a revolutionary way of riding

indicators.note: something revolutionary overturns the order, so these letters are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rider describes a radical new technique while sitting on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitation is the formal term for horsemanship, the art and manner of riding a horse.

indicators.note: encompasses says the phrase before it holds the answer, the it of the clue, inside its letters

explanation.surface: Someone supposes that a broad dyke wraps around something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encompasses it' means the words 'wide embankment' contain the answer, running across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem something is to judge or consider it so, a formal synonym for believe.

clue.text: Violent storm, it comes before last character goes to tourist centre

indicators.note: violent suggests the storm is thrown about, rearranging its letters

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A fierce storm arrives before the final guest reaches a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes before' and 'goes to' are link phrases ordering the pieces; the last character is the alphabet's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: St Moritz is a famous Swiss resort, a ski destination drawing many tourists.

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient
VEN abbreviates Venerable, the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: An Eastern churchman of high rank stands motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon in the Church of England is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: still and even both mean calm and smooth, as in still or even waters.

indicators.note: read as re-move, so the letters are moved again into another order

parts.note: something trendy is in

explanation.surface: A man can take off a fashionable fetter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to enchain someone is to bind them in chains, to shackle them.

clue.text: Half of them fellows get story right about cheese

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is two of its letters, here the back half

parts.note: fellows are men
a story is a tale

explanation.surface: Half the men get a tale right about a cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of them' takes the back half, EM.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmentaler is the Swiss holey cheese, more often spelt Emmental.

parts.note: a goon is a thug or hoodlum

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles gangster ends up in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagoon is a stretch of shallow water cut off from the sea, a kind of lake.

indicators.note: said says the word is to be spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: a bridle path is a track for horse riders, so path calls up bridle

explanation.surface: Someone talks about the aisle walked at weddings.
explanation.walkthrough: A bridle path or bridleway is a British track for horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal is the adjective for a bride or a wedding, so it means of weddings.

clue.text: Fire group of people in which competitors are at a handicap

definitions.text: in which competitors are at a handicap

parts.note: to fire someone from a job is to sack them
a race is a group of people of shared descent

explanation.surface: Dismissing a whole group of people puts competitors at a disadvantage.
explanation.definitionFit: In this school sports-day contest runners hop along with both legs inside a sack, a deliberate handicap.

indicators.note: after puts the reworked leg behind the run in the answer

parts.note: to jog is to run gently

indicators.note: injured suggests the word leg is damaged and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A jogger's injured leg starts trembling after the run.
explanation.definitionFit: To joggle is to shake or jolt something slightly, a close synonym.

clue.text: Some significant earnings expected from stake

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gambler hopes a big win will follow from the money put down.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'expected from stake' is too long: only 'stake' means the answer, and 'expected from' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is the stake each poker player puts in before the deal.

indicators.note: waved suggests letters flapped about, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thumped while a girl named Dawn waved.
explanation.definitionFit: Up and down the country means throughout it, so the phrase stands for everywhere in a place.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: A Welshman who is a single professional.
explanation.definitionFit: Ifor is a traditional Welsh male name, so it serves as an example of a Welshman.

clue.text: It doesn't come as much of a blow

definitions.text: It doesn't come as much of a blow

parts.words: It doesn't come as much of a blow
parts.note: sounds like news that is no great shock, but blow here is a gust of wind, and a mild one

explanation.definitionFit: On the Beaufort scale this force-three wind is light, hardly a strong blow at all.
